title: How Close Will Gliese 710 Come to the Sun?
description:
What Happens When a Star Passes Through Our Solar System?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-jImX5h7ws

Gaia measurements put Gliese 710's closest approach at about a fifth of a light-year — roughly 13,000 times the Earth–Sun distance. If the gap between the Sun and Earth were one centimetre, Neptune would sit 30 centimetres away on a ruler, and Gliese 710 would pass more than 100 metres away, the length of a football pitch.

Sources: Bailer-Jones (2022), The Astrophysical Journal Letters 935 L9 — Gaia DR3 closest-approach distance of 10,635–16,649 AU (~0.21 light-years) (https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac816a) · Berski & Dybczyński (2016), Astronomy & Astrophysics 595 L10 — Gliese 710 encounter and Oort Cloud scale (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201629835).

Pictures: NASA/JPL Voyager 2 full-disk photograph of Neptune (PIA01492), alongside original animated explainers, AI-generated scenes, and AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/JPL.
